hook.speaker: Krishna (quoted by Bhishma)

hook.line: Harsh words from family can keep burning long after they're said. Even Krishna felt it.
hook.translation: My heart is churned the way someone wanting fire churns a fire-stick. The harsh words my relatives say keep burning me, day after day.
hook.why: In family feuds, the weapon that works is gentleness, patience and respect.

prasang.title: Krishna's family troubles: the weapon not made of iron
prasang.summary: Even Krishna struggles with his clan: he does their work, bears their harsh words, and feels like the mother of two gamblers playing each other. Narada tells him the only weapon that works is soft: generosity, patience, sincerity, gentleness and respect.
prasang.story_hook: Krishna, who guided a war, admitted to a sage that he could not keep the peace in his own family.
prasang.lesson: In family feuds, the weapon that works is gentleness, patience and respect.

alternates.speaker: Tulsidas
alternates.sanskrit: जासु भरोसें सोइऐे राखि गोद में सीस। तुलसी तासु कुचाल तें रखवारो जगदीस॥
alternates.line: When the person you trusted most turns on you, the Lord of the world still guards you.
alternates.translation: When the one you trusted enough to sleep with your head in their lap turns on you, Tulsi says, the Lord of the world is your guardian.
alternates.misuse: Comfort after betrayal; it does not replace getting real-world help or protection.

alternates.speaker: Vibhishan
alternates.setting: Vibhishan, Ravana's good-hearted brother, describes his life in Ravana's court.
alternates.sanskrit: सुनहु पवनसुत रहनि हमारी। जिमि दसनन्हि महुँ जीभ बिचारी॥ तात कबहुँ मोहि जानि अनाथा। करिहहिं कृपा भानुकुल नाथा ॥
alternates.line: I live here like the tongue among the teeth.
alternates.translation: Son of the wind, hear how I live: like the poor tongue among the teeth. Friend, knowing me to be without support, will the Lord of the Sun dynasty ever show me grace?
alternates.why: Even in a hostile place there may be one ally; find them.

prasang.title: Hanuman finds a friend in Lanka
prasang.summary: Searching Lanka, Hanuman is surprised to find a house with Ram's name on it. Its owner, Vibhishan, Ravana's brother, says he lives in Lanka like a tongue among teeth. Hanuman tells him even a restless monkey like himself was given Ram's love.
prasang.story_hook: In a city of demons, Hanuman heard someone wake up and say Ram's name.
prasang.lesson: Even in a hostile place there may be one ally; find them.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna addresses the Kaurava court, asking Dhritarashtra to restrain his sons and make peace.
verse.sanskrit: धर्मज्ञेषु सभासत्सु नेह युक्तमसांप्रतम् / यत्र धर्मो ह्यधर्मेण सत्यं यत्रानृतेन च हन्यते प्रेक्षमाणानां हतास्तत्र सभासदः / विद्धो धर्मो ह्यधर्मेण सभां यत्र प्रपद्यते
verse.line: When wrong crushes right while others watch in silence, the silent are wounded too.
verse.translation: Where right is struck down by wrong and truth by falsehood while the assembly looks on, it is the onlookers who are struck down.
verse.why: You can make the best case for peace and still be refused. Speak anyway.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते । स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥
verse.line: No sincere effort here is ever wasted. Even a little of it shields you from great fear.
verse.translation: On this path no effort is lost and no harm results. Even a little of this practice protects one from great fear.

words.en: here no stepping back, no destruction

verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.meaning: On this path, no beginning is lost and no harm results. Even a small amount of this practice protects from great fear. The tradition reads this as a path of action where every step forward counts, and even a little effort shields one from the fear of birth and death.
verse.for_you: Twenty-two years of service were not erased in a ten-minute call. Even a little of this steady practice shields you from great fear.
verse.try_today: Notice one small task today done without clinging to the result.

why: answers the worry that an unfinished effort is a wasted one
Even a little of this path protects from great fear.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
verse.sanskrit: सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत् । सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः ॥
verse.line: Don't abandon work that suits you just because it has flaws. Every undertaking has some, like fire has smoke.
verse.translation: One should not give up the work suited to one's nature, Kaunteya, even if it has faults; for all undertakings are clouded by faults, as fire is by smoke.
verse.why: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.
verse.misuse: Not 'never change jobs'. It answers perfectionism, not a reason to stay where you're harmed.

prasang.title: Duties by nature, and their fruit
prasang.summary: After listing duties by varna, Krishna says one reaches perfection through one's own work done as worship, and that one's own path, though imperfect, beats another's, since every undertaking has flaws.
prasang.lesson: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.

verse.for_you: You have spent twenty-two years in one place. The work suited you, and its flaws did not stop you. A single meeting does not erase the life you built there.
verse.try_today: Notice the work you were born to do today.

why: flaws in the work are no reason to drop it; every undertaking has them
keeps a resolve from breaking on the first flaw

verse.speaker: Vidura
verse.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verse.sanskrit: निश्चित्य यः प्रक्रमते नान्तर्वसति कर्मणः / अवन्ध्यकालो वश्यात्मा स वै पण्डित उच्यते
verse.line: Decide, then begin. Don't stall halfway, don't waste time, and keep yourself steady.
verse.translation: One who begins only after deciding, does not stop halfway through the work, does not waste time and keeps himself in hand, is called wise.
verse.why: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

prasang.title: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool
prasang.summary: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
prasang.lesson: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

verse.for_you: You have already decided to stay steady even when the ground under you was pulled away. Let that decision be enough to carry you through this morning and the rest of the day.
verse.try_today: Notice one small thing today that you decide to do without hesitation and carry it through to the end.
verse.scene_line: In the quiet before dawn, you stand steady like Vidura before the king, waiting to see what the next move will be.

why: Reflect fully, then decide and begin.
Nishchitya: begin from a settled decision

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha teaches the disheartened young Rama that effort, not fate, shapes his life.
verse.line: When your mind drifts to harmful things, steer it back to good ones. That's the whole teaching.
verse.translation: When the mind has sunk into bad things, bring it down into good ones with effort. That is the summary of all the scriptures.
verse.why: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

prasang.title: Vasishtha on self-effort: fate is only your past effort
prasang.summary: Vasishtha's first teaching to Rama is a long case for self-effort. What people call fate is simply the fruit of their own past effort, and present effort can overcome it, as the stronger of two rams wins. He also says not to torment yourself over what was beyond your power, and to steer your habits gently, like raising a child.
prasang.lesson: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

verse.try_today: Steer your mind back to the good, each time it drifts toward harm.

why: turn the mind back each time

story.title: Jaratkaru's wife must choose between his anger and his duty
story.story_hook: If she woke him, he would be furious. If she did not, he would fail his duty. She had until sunset.
story.summary: Her husband married her on the condition that he would leave the first time she displeased him. Now he is asleep with his head in her lap and the sun is going down. If she wakes him he will be angry. If she lets him sleep he will miss his evening rites.
story.lesson: When both paths carry a cost, choose by which loss is heavier, and say plainly why you chose.
story.teaser: If she woke him, he would be furious. If she did not, he would fail his duty. She had until sunset.
story.for_you: You were let go with no respect. You still wake at six for a place that no longer holds you. Choose the loss that is heavier, and say plainly why you chose it.
